headlines.headline: Giants try to end 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia, as Eagles turn to 3rd-string QB Milton
headlines.description: — The New York Giants could practically mark an ‘L’ on their schedule each season as soon as they saw their date in Philadelphia.
headlines.title: Giants try to end 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia, as Eagles turn to 3rd-string QB Milton
headlines.linkText: Giants try to end 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia, as Eagles turn to 3rd-string QB Milton
headlines.story: PHILADELPHIA -- — The New York Giants could practically mark an ‘L’ on their schedule each season as soon as they saw their date in Philadelphia. It's been automatic. The Eagles have beaten the Giants 13 straight times at home — including one playoff win — since New York last won on Oct. 27, 2013. Maybe not this season. The Giants (4-2-1) come to Philadelphia on Sunday as betting favorites and in first place in the woeful NFC East. If the Giants win, they'd practically have a stranglehold in a division where no other team has a winning record, and they have yet to lose to Washington or Dallas. Are the Giants getting cocky and complacent in coach John Harbaugh's first season? “I do think that that’s definitely something to get locked in on,” Harbaugh said, “but I don’t believe it is this week.” Long the class of the NFC East, the Eagles (2-6) are on a six-game losing streak and set to start their third quarterback of the season — the fourth one who'll take snaps. Eagles coach Nick Sirianni had promised that everything was on the table when it came to trying to get his team rolling again. He instead kept beleaguered offensive coordinator Sean Mannion as the play-caller but benched Tanner McKee after he went 0-3 since taking over as the starter when Jalen Hurts was sidelined for the season because of blood clots. The move came roughly 48 hours after Sirianni said McKee was their guy and a change at the position was not coming. Joe Milton is now tasked with saving the Eagles' season. Just maybe the Eagles could see a path toward a division title if they knock off the Giants. NFL history suggests it's unlikely. Only three teams that started 2-6 have ever made the playoffs. The 26-year-old Milton has appeared in five NFL games in relief, including Dallas’ season finale at the Giants in January, when he was 7 of 13 for 73 yards and an interception. “He works extremely hard,” Sirianni said. “He’s always in the building doing the extra things, and I like his progression.” Milton was oh-so briefly a teammate with Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy in 2020 at Michigan. Milton transferred to Tennessee while McCarthy would lead the Wolverines to a national title. Much like the Eagles, the Giants have churned through quarterbacks, going from Jaxson Dart (injured) to Jameis Winston (benched) before settling on McCarthy. He'll make his second start of the season, a veteran compared to Milton's first career start after mostly playing garbage time in two previous stops. Milton’s job is to give the Eagles at least a glimmer of hope of keeping their playoff hopes alive. The Giants follow the Eagles with a home game Thursday night against Washington. The teams already played to a tie. If the Giants win both games against their rivals, the division crown is all but headed up the turnpike. Up first: ending a very unlucky 13-game losing streak in Philadelphia. The Giants suddenly have the opportunity to bury the Eagles in their own division. “It’s all kind of meaningless,” Harbaugh said. “I mean, if you’re betting, it’s important, but it doesn’t matter to us because there’s still 10 games left to play. And I’m quite sure every one of the teams in the division believes that in those 10 games, they can make up ground.” Need to know New York Giants (4-2-1) at Philadelphia (2-6) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EDT, Fox. Latest odds: Giants by 3 1/2. Against the spread: Giants 5-2; Eagles 1-7. Last week: Giants had a bye; Eagles lost to the Commanders 27-10. Last meeting: Eagles beat the Giants 38-20 on Oct. 26, 2025, in Philadelphia. Series record: Eagles lead 93-87-2. Matchup to watch Milton vs. the Giants' defense. Milton is regarded as having a cannon for an arm, but that hasn't earned him much playing time in the NFL. He has attempted only 53 passes the last two seasons with two teams and will only have four days of practice headed into the game with Philadelphia's first-team offense. The Giants are third in the NFL in pass defense and could thrive against an Eagles team that has been outscored by a whopping 65 points through eight games. The Eagles are 27th in the league in passing offense at 177.1 yards per game. Stats and stuff — Harbaugh during his 18 seasons with Baltimore was 15-3 after a bye, a winning percentage of .833 that's the best of any coach in the Super Bowl era. — The Giants and Eagles split the series last season. — The Eagles have not had more than 341 yards of total offense in a game this season. They hit that mark in Week 2 against Tennessee. It was Philadelphia's last win of the season. They've averaged 244 yards per game over their six-game losing streak. — The Eagles' Braden Mann leads the NFL with 20 punts inside the 20-yard line. — Philadelphia is 16-4 (.800) in its last 20 games vs. New York. — The Giants have scored 27-plus points in four straight games dating to Week 4. It's the most consecutive games scoring 27-plus points by the Giants since 2010. — The Giants have forced 32 three-and-outs this year, tied for the second most in the NFL. — The Eagles will have had four quarterbacks attempt a pass in a season for the first time since 1991. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.headline: Stumbling Texans and winless Chargers meet in a matchup of NFL disappointments
headlines.description: — The Houston Texans and Los Angeles...
headlines.title: Stumbling Texans and winless Chargers meet in a matchup of NFL disappointments
headlines.linkText: Stumbling Texans and winless Chargers meet in a matchup of NFL disappointments
headlines.story: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — The Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers began the season with legitimate playoff and Super Bowl expectations. After stumbling through the first half, they're in salvage mode as two of the biggest disappointments in the NFL. The Texans made the playoffs three years in a row — a franchise best — and won the AFC South two of those years before opening this season 0-4. The Chargers won 11 games and reached the playoffs in each of coach Jim Harbaugh's first two seasons, but are the league's only remaining winless team. The underperformers meet Sunday at SoFi Stadium. The Texans (2-5) are happily on the road coming off their bye week, having gone 0-4 at home. The Chargers (0-7) have dropped 10 straight overall dating to last season. “We’ve been in a lot of close games,” Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said. “How do you find yourself on the winning side of those games? Being great in situational football and finishing the proper way. If we do those things, that’s when you earn the right to win games.” No team starting 0-7 or worse has ever made the NFL playoffs. At this point, the Bolts would settle for a touchdown. They've gone nine quarters and 27 drives without one. Their last came in the third quarter of a 23-17 loss to Denver on Oct. 11. “Want to win, want to get the ball in the end zone,” coach Jim Harbaugh said. “Focused on getting it turned, forging ahead and really striving in every way to play winning football.” The Chargers failed to show signs of life coming out of their Week 7 bye, losing to the Los Angeles Rams 24-9 last weekend. Justin Herbert passed for a season-best 257 yards, but also had two more interceptions, giving him a league-high 10 for the season. He has thrown at least one in every game so far. Conversely, Houston QB C.J. Stroud is among the league's top passers, with 11 TDs and just one interception. The Texans' self-inflicted wounds include a non-existent ground game and foolish penalties. "Focus on the little things, fix those, and I think we'll be fine,” said Stroud, who spent last weekend in Los Angeles watching his alma mater Ohio State get upset by USC. The Texans have lost wide receiver Jaylin Noel (turf toe) for the season after he got hurt in a 27-21 overtime loss to the New York Giants. He generated explosiveness on offense and production as a kick and punt returner. “We’re going to feel it,” Stroud said. “It sucks that he’s starting to really find himself and then to go down like that.” Harbaugh is 0-7 as a coach for the first time, but he endured an identical stretch of losing as quarterback for the Chargers in 2000 when they began 0-7 in San Diego. That team finished 1-15. “Stay motivated, stay dedicated, all of us doing our job to the best of our ability,” Harbaugh said. “The things that aren’t coming easy, that’s what you push through until it does, until you make it happen on a consistent basis.” Need to know Houston (2-5) at Los Angeles Chargers (0-7) When/where to watch: Sunday, 4 p.m. EST, CBS. Latest odds: Texans by 4 1/2. Against the spread: Texans 2-5; Chargers 0-5-1. Last week: Texans had bye week; Chargers lost to the Rams 24-9. Last meeting: Texans beat Chargers 20-16 on Dec. 27, 2025, in Inglewood, California. Series record: Chargers lead Texans 6-4. Matchup to watch Houston DE Will Anderson Jr. and the Texans' pass rush vs. the Chargers' mostly rookie offensive line. Anderson is tied for the league lead in sacks with 7 1/2 and will be looking to exploit the Bolts' inexperienced line protecting Herbert. The QB has been sacked 23 times, tied for the second-most in the league. Stats and stuff — The Chargers continue to be without starting S Derwin James Jr. (hamstring), who's on injured reserve and won't be eligible to play again until Nov. 29. He has been limited to three games. — Houston has forced five turnovers in the last two games against the Chargers, including the postseason. — The Texans are tied for the fifth-most sacks (21) and have the fifth-highest quarterback pressure rate (37.4%) in the AFC. — The Chargers are 0-4 at SoFi Stadium this season, with their last home win in December 2025. — Houston's three turnovers are the tied for the fewest in the league. — Stroud joins Detroit's Jared Goff as the only quarterbacks to throw for over 1,500 yards and one or fewer interceptions this season. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.headline: Panthers place focus on stopping the run vs. Broncos following defensive coordinator change
headlines.description: — Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales offered one overriding requisition to Todd Wash after promoting him to interim defensive coordinator last week: "Stop the run."
headlines.title: Panthers place focus on stopping the run vs. Broncos following defensive coordinator change
headlines.linkText: Panthers place focus on stopping the run vs. Broncos following defensive coordinator change
headlines.story: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- — Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales offered one overriding requisition to Todd Wash after promoting him to interim defensive coordinator last week: "Stop the run." That's something the Panthers struggled to do under Ejiro Evero, and it ultimately cost him his job. The Panthers (3-4) enter Sunday's game against the surging Denver Broncos (6-2) ranked 30th in the league against the run, while allowing the fifth-most points in the league. It's now up to Wash to fix it. Canales made the change at coordinator just hours after the Panthers suffered their second straight loss last Thursday night to the Green Packers, 27-19. The timing of the move gave Wash a few extra days to make changes. Just how dramatically different the Panthers will look on Sunday remains to be seen, as players and coaches alike have been predictably coy when it comes to the game plan. “I guess we will have to see Sunday,” defensive lineman Derrick Brown said with a grin. There's speculation the Panthers could begin to transition away from Evero's 3-4 base scheme to the 4-3 scheme Wash used during his previous stint as an NFL defensive coordinator with the Jacksonville Jaguars (2016-2020). But Brown said that's easier said than done in the middle of an NFL season. “I don’t think that’s what we’re doing,” Brown said the idea of shifting to a base 4-3 defense, “So it’s one of those things where we just got a few different tweaks here and there, but for the most part we’re going to do what we did.” Wash seemed to echo that sentiment, while still leaving the door open to change. “We are who we are,” Wash said in reference to the team's defensive personnel which is made up heavily of outside linebackers. “(But) we will try to throw some wrinkles in.” The Broncos enter the game on a four-game win streak despite an offense that ranks 30th in the league overall and 26th in rushing. However, Bo Nix and company seem to be hitting their stride. Denver has scored 58 points over the past two weeks. Jonah Coleman took on a bigger role in the backfield in the Broncos' 28-24 come-from-behind win over Kansas City, rushing 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching four passes for 63 yards. Nix's latest comeback propelled the Broncos into sole possession of first place in the AFC West. The Panthers (3-4) are also alone in first in the NFC South despite a losing record. Nix described the Broncos as being a “mature team" and isn't expecting a letdown against Carolina. “Coach (Sean) Payton talks about every game in the NFL is an important game and there’s no such thing as a trap game because they’re all that way,” Nix said. “They’re all must wins. If you don’t play well, you’re going to end up messing around and getting beat. We know the importance of this week right before the bye. We can’t go on a bye early.” Need to know Denver (6-2) at Carolina (3-4). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m., EST, CBS. Latest odds: Broncos by 3. Against the spread: Broncos 6-2, Panthers 3-4. Last week: Broncos beat Chiefs 28-24; Panthers lost to Packers 27-19. Last meeting: Broncos beat Panthers 28-14 on Oct. 27, 2024, in Denver. Series record: Broncos lead 6-2. Matchup to watch Broncos pass rush vs. Panthers QB Bryce Young. Young spent most of last week's Thursday night's game trying to escape constant pressure. He was sacked six times and forced to throw the ball away early on a number of occasions by the Packers. Green Bay was able to bat down passes and get to Young using a basic four-man rush. The Broncos are expected to borrow a page from the Packers playbook as they look to take advantage of a Carolina offensive line without three starters. Denver is tied for fourth in the league with 23 sacks entering Week 9. The most significant was Malcolm Roach's last-second sack on Patrick Mahomes to seal Denver's win over the Chiefs. Stats and stuff — The Broncos beat the Panthers 24-10 in Super Bowl 50 on Feb. 7, 2016, in Santa Clara, California. — Nix has 15 game-winning drives and 12 fourth-quarter comebacks since entering the NFL in 2024, both of which lead the league in that span. — Denver has won 15 consecutive one-score regular-season games going back to last season. — Broncos K Wil Lutz owns the longest streak of extra point conversions (113) since the league moved the PAT back in 2015. — Denver ILB Alex Singleton, the league’s tackling leader, has consecutive games with 14 tackles and a sack, something that’s been accomplished just two other times since 1987 (LB Ray Lewis in 2001, LB Micheal Barrow in 1998). — Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins has 306 yards on 94 carries, and his 3.3 yard per carry average ranks second worst in the league among players with at least 90 carries. — Young will start his 52nd career game with the Panthers, surpassing Steve Beuerlein for the third-most starts by a QB in team history. Only Cam Newton (129) and Jake Delhomme (90) have more. — Panthers WR Tetairoa McMillan has been fairly quiet since his 14-catch, 192-yard, two-touchdown performance against the Lions on Oct. 4. In the three games that have followed, he has a combined 184 yards on 16 receptions and no TDs. — Panthers K Ryan Fitzgerald has started the season 13-for-13 on field-goal attempts. Fitzgerald is one of four kickers in the league to remain perfect with a minimum of at least 10 field-goal attempts. ------ AP Pro Football Writer Arnie Stapleton in Denver contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.story: INDIANAPOLIS -- — Jonathan Taylor has grown accustomed to playing football as the rumor mill spins. This week, he has heard his named linked to multiple teams, heard about “done deals” and heard some question whether it's wise to even play Sunday when the struggling Indianapolis Colts and Dallas Cowboys meet — two days before this season's trade deadline. So Taylor has learned how to laugh it off. All he wants to do is give the fans something to cheer. “It's kind of dragged on for a while now, so at this point, it's just noise,” Taylor said Thursday about the chatter. “It's been like three or four or however many weeks, so at this point, it becomes regular scheduled programming.” It wasn't supposed to be this way after the seven-year veteran who has never played for another team signed a two-year contract extension worth $44 million to stay with the Colts in August. Even then, this week's featured matchup was supposed to be about the brother bash: Indy's veteran receiver Josh Downs and Cowboys rookie safety Caleb Downs. But with both teams reeling, the older brother requesting a trade and the younger brother in the concussion protocol and dealing with a bad ankle, their dream story may have to wait. That puts the spotlight on Taylor, the franchise's No. 2 career rusher in what could be his final game playing in the Colts — though it's not something he has contemplated. “We've got an opportunity, especially this week — especially after last week — to come back and put a better product on the field,” he said, referring to the embarrassing 42-7 loss to Jacksonville. “That's my biggest goal. Last week was tough. You know you never want to go and put that on display." He just wants to give fans something to cheer about. Indy has (2-6) lost four straight and 13 of 15 and the last time they were home, the boobirds were out in force. Dallas (3-5) hasn't played much better lately. It has the league's worst run defense and has lost three of four after blowing a lead and losing 33-30 in overtime at Arizona last week. So coach Brian Schottenheimer would like nothing better than to ruin Indy's homecoming — even if it Taylor's last stand. “There are certainly a lot of things we as a football team can do better," he said, noting the Cowboys' rushing disparity from Week 7 to Week 8. “I didn’t think we did a great job tackling. And then there’s certainly things that I can do better in all facets, No. 1 being find a way to finish the game and give us a chance.” Need to know Dalals (3-5) at Indianapolis (2-6) When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, Fox. Latest odds: Cowboys by 5½. Against the spread: Cowboys 4-4; Colts 4-4. Last week: Cowboys lost to Cardinals 33-30 in OT; Colts lost to Jaguars 42-7. Last meeting: Cowboys beat Colts 54-19 on Dec. 4, 2022, in Dallas. Series record: Cowboys lead 11-6. Matchup to watch Cowboys pass defense vs. Colts QB Daniel Jones. With the uncertainty around Taylor after a season-low eight carries last week, the more determinative matchup may be the turnover-prone Jones against a team ranked in the bottom five in takeaways (six). Jones has lost four fumbles, thrown nine interceptions and has at least one INT in seven games this year. Stats and stuff — The Colts and Cowboys faced each another three times before the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, then met again in Super Bowl 5, a 16-13 Colts victory when the team was still in Baltimore. — Dallas has only one win outside Texas this season. It came at Philadelphia in Week 6. — WR CeeDee Lamb is one of three players entering Week 9 with 60 catches and he became the first player in franchise history to reach that mark in eight games or fewer. — QB Dak Prescott has thrown at least one TD pass in every game this season, a personal best streak to start a season. — Indy is playing at home for the first time since general manager Chris Ballard was fired and Pro Bowlers Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner were traded. — WR Keenan Allen needs four catches to pass Tim Brown for No. 8 on the NFL's career list. Brown had 1,094 during during his Hall of Fame career. Allen has 29 catches in his last five games. — Taylor ranks eighth in the NFL in yards rushing (610) and is tied for third with eight TD runs. — Indy is tied for last in the league in takeaways (four) and has the worst turnover margin at minus-11. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.story:
There are two factors that go into determining the best and worst fantasy football landing spots for Jonathan Taylor.

The first is what is best for Taylor. I fully believe he is an elite talent and will succeed anywhere. And any team trading for him has to be in a better situation than the Indianapolis Colts, who have traded their top offensive lineman. They have also had poor quarterback play and often trail, which means a negative game script for the running game. However, Taylor is also going to crater the fantasy value of the running backs on whichever team he is dealt to. That should be considered as well.

Best Jonathan Taylor landing spots

1. Minnesota Vikings: I would expect any team that acquires Taylor to use him plenty, but the Vikings and their style of play make a lot of sense. They have run the ball at the sixth-highest rate this season. They want to establish the run and trust their defense. Minnesota has created the third-most yards before contact on RB carries, so its offensive line is creating running lanes for the backs.

This is a situation where Taylor would get to come in and become the immediate focal point on a team very much in the hunt. It could also help open things up in the passing game, which Justin Jefferson managers would enjoy. Lastly, neither of the Vikings' current running backs is a great fantasy option. Since Jordan Mason returned, neither he nor Aaron Jones Sr. has scored seven fantasy points in a game.

2. Seattle Seahawks: This would ruin the fantasy values of Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet, but neither has provided much anyway. The Seahawks have struggled to create consistent running lanes, as evidenced by their 0.6 yards before contact per carry (NFL average: 0.9); however, we should see improvements there with recent acquisition Quenton Nelson on the offensive line. This is the rare instance where Taylor would not be the focal point of opposing defenses, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba on the perimeter.

3. Cincinnati Bengals: This would hurt in fantasy as it would take Chase Brown out as a weekly option. However, the Bengals' offense would be the NFL version of the "Monstars" with Taylor added. Good luck stacking the box and leaving Tee Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase to run wild in the secondary.

4. Washington Commanders: The Commanders are creating running lanes, but their backs have struggled to consistently produce. Taylor would immediately change that, on a team that has a ton of touches up for grabs. Taylor getting to run the option with Jayden Daniels should make fantasy managers of either player salivate. We have yet to see Daniels paired with a dominant running back.

5. New England Patriots: The Patriots' backs might produce at times for fantasy, but they have struggled all season. Both Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson have averaged under 4 yards per carry. In fact, both have negative rush EPAs on the season. Taylor would come in, see the bulk of work, and give New England potentially three elite offensive players when A.J. Brown returns.

Worst Jonathan Taylor landing spots

1. Denver Broncos: My answer for the worst fantasy landing spot for Taylor might surprise some. The Broncos are struggling on the ground despite a strong offensive line. They rank just above league average in yards before contact, and their current backs have picked up yards after contact at the lowest rate in the NFL and explosive runs at the fifth-lowest rate. Taylor would elevate this, but my biggest concern is usage.

Under Sean Payton, the Broncos have been more of a "sum of their parts" offense. Perhaps acquiring Taylor would change that, but people said the same thing when the team acquired Jaylen Waddle. Taylor would obviously see the most touches for Denver, but would we see the other backs mixed in and eating into his workload? Fantasy managers have long been burned by Payton's unpredictable shenanigans.

Plus, this would wreck the fantasy value of Jonah Coleman, who has the potential to be a breakout star this season. Coleman ranks third among running backs in explosive run rate and has shown to be the most effective Broncos RB in the running and passing games. He has league-winning upside if he gets to remain as the lead back.

2. Green Bay Packers: The Packers make sense given Josh Jacobs' off-the-field situation; however, they have been vocal that they expect him to remain with the team. Green Bay is tied for the second-fewest yards before contact per carry (0.4). Its offensive line has struggled to create running lanes all season. Plus, the Packers have found their most success since Jordan Love began airing the ball out. Between the offensive line struggles and Jacobs' presence, this would not be a great landing spot.

3. New York Giants: Taylor would produce anywhere, but to varying degrees. The Giants have created 0.5 rushing yards before contact per carry, which is tied for the fourth lowest in the NFL. I'd expect him to see a heavy dose of stacked boxes here, as the Giants' passing attack isn't scaring opposing defenses like with other teams listed here. Plus, there is the pressure to perform in New York and the fact that this would tank Cam Skattebo's fantasy value.

headlines.story:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice filed for bankruptcy in federal court Wednesday, claiming he has more than $3.45 million in debts, according to federal court records.

Rice, who filed in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, claimed more than $2.1 million of his debts are tied to varying plaintiffs suing him in civil litigations that have either been settled or are awaiting trial.

Rice, 26, has been sued by multiple individuals for his role in a high-speed multicar crash in Dallas in 2024 and an ex-girlfriend alleging he repeatedly assaulted her from 2023 to 2025.

In the filing, Rice claimed to have $677,054 in personal assets, including $421,825 in "deferred compensation." The filing claims Rice has $13,640 in his checking accounts. He claims to rent a residence and that he does not own any property.

Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which is for "individuals who have financial difficulty preventing them from paying their debts and who are willing to allow their non-exempt property to be used to pay their creditors," according to the bankruptcy filing. Rice claimed $39,241 of his personal assets to be nonexempt.

The documents claim Rice's largest creditor is still owed $979,837 as part of a 2025 civil settlement related to the crash. Rice is disputing potential debts in some of the civil trials, including a combined $700,000 in lawsuits filed by 2024 crash victims and $200,000 as part of the alleged assault suit.

According to the documents, Rice used his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral with Thomas McMurray, his attorney in the pending civil litigations.

Rice's bankruptcy attorney, David Shuster, and the Chiefs had no comment about the bankruptcy filing. McMurray did not immediately respond to messages left by ESPN seeking comment.

Rice is in the final year of his rookie contract with the Chiefs and is expected to make $1,560,711 in base salary in 2026. He has played in five games this season, with 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns.

headlines.story:
While Week 8 meant the debut of two "Rivalries" jerseys, another alternate look returns to the field in Week 9, and a popular throwback comes back. 

The Los Angeles Chargers are wearing their "Super Chargers" all-navy threads against the Houston Texans. Unveiled in 2025, the Chargers deemed the navy uniforms "a true modern throwback." It's a nod to threads worn in the 1990s and early 2000s, which coincided with a Super Bowl XXIX appearance and four AFC West titles. The navy jersey includes white modern numbers with an old-school outline and gold trim. The navy pants boast a bolt on the side, while a bolt also runs on the shoulders and helmet. "Super Chargers" is stitched in white on the neckline. 

In a trend that's becoming more common around the league, the New York Giants and Philadelphia Eagles offer a matchup of throwback uniforms. The Eagles are rocking their "Kelly Green" threads, while it's a "Vintage White" look for the Giants. "Thursday Night Football" between the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks in Week 6 also brought a throwback threads matchup. Philadelphia brought back the iconic Kelly Green combination in 2023, while New York's look returned in 2025 after a one-year hiatus. 

Alternates are still represented well throughout the week, though.

The Baltimore Ravens are wearing their "Purple Rising" combination on "Thursday Night Football" against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Baltimore unveiled the look in the offseason as part of their wardrobe overhaul. It includes a new "Purple Rising" helmet, first introduced in 2024 with the alternate purple jersey. The primary logo appears on the metallic purple lid instead of the front-facing Ravens one. Different from the previous all-purple combination is a new "midnight purple" color, which is meant to emulate the iridescence of a raven's feather, and "Purple Rising" running on the inside collar.

The New Orleans Saints are going gold against the Cleveland Browns. And it's another navy look for the Dallas Cowboys against the Indianapolis Colts, who are doing a rare home white out. 

Here's a look at the Week 9 uniforms for all NFL teams, excluding the Pittsburgh Steelers and Tennessee Titans, who are on a bye.

headlines.headline: The Raiders make their return to the Bay Area when they take on the 49ers
headlines.description: — Maxx Crosby is one of the few remaining players on the Raiders with ties to the team's old home in Oakland, making this week's trip to play the
headlines.title: The Raiders make their return to the Bay Area when they take on the 49ers
headlines.linkText: The Raiders make their return to the Bay Area when they take on the 49ers
headlines.story: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- — Maxx Crosby is one of the few remaining players on the Raiders with ties to the team's old home in Oakland, making this week's trip to play the San Francisco 49ers extra special. The Raiders (4-4) will play their first regular-season game in the Bay Area since moving from Oakland to Las Vegas after the 2019 season when they visit the 49ers (6-1) on Sunday. Crosby is one of three remaining Raiders who played in Oakland — along with tackle Kolton Miller and punter AJ Cole — and looks forward to the chance to play in front of some of those old fans who still travel to some of their games. “I know definitely being in the Bay, there’s going to be a lot of tension in the air and a lot excitement at the same time,” said Crosby, who was a rookie in the Raiders' last season in Oakland in 2019. “It’s special just being a part of that rivalry and just knowing the history, taking your time to really understand what that comes from and how important it was to all the fans.” The teams have met once since the Raiders moved with San Francisco winning 37-34 in overtime in Las Vegas in Week 17 of the 2022 season. The previous time they played in the Bay came in 2018 when the Niners won 34-3 in a Week 9 game played between a pair of one-win teams going nowhere. There's much more optimism this time with the 49ers at the top of the NFC standings despite losing their first game two weeks ago in Atlanta before a bye week and the Raiders coming in with a .500 record after beating the New York Jets last week. That will only add to the intensity for both the players and the fans of both teams, who still harbor animosity over the decades of sharing a home market. “It’s exciting for me because I know it’s exciting for the fans,” San Francisco linebacker Fred Warner said. “I’ve had several people on the outside tell me, man, y’all better beat the Raiders. So it means a lot even though they aren’t in Oakland anymore this week. They’re the Oakland Raiders this week, and so it’s an exciting man. I know it’ll be packed in there.” Need to know Las Vegas (4-4) vs. San Francisco (6-1) When/where to watch: Sunday, 4:25 p.m. EST, Fox. Latest odds: 49ers by 9 1/2. Against the spread: Raiders 6-2; 49ers 4-3. Last week: Raiders beat the New York Jets 38-33; 49ers had bye, lost 29-20 to Atlanta on Oct. 25. Last meeting: 49ers beat Raiders 37-34 in OT on Jan. 1, 2023, in Las Vegas. Series record: 49ers lead 8-7. Matchup to watch Raiders TE Brock Bowers vs. 49ers pass defense. San Francisco allowed 18 catches for 127 yards by tight ends the past two weeks and now must match up with one of the game's best in Bowers. Bowers is the first tight end with at least 70 yards receiving in his first six games in a season and his 217 career catches are four shy of Trey McBride's record for a tight end in his first three seasons. Stats and stuff — The Raiders have scored 89 more points through eight games than last season. First-year coach Klint Kubiak is the fourth coach since the merger in 1970 to register that kind of improvement as well as four or more victories. The others were the Baltimore Colts’ Ted Marchibroda in 1978, Los Angeles Rams’ Sean McVay in 2017 and Chicago’s Matt Nagy in 2018. — Kirk Cousins is the first Raiders quarterback with at least 2,000 yards passing (2,124) and 20 total touchdowns passing and running in the first eight games of a season. — The 221 points scored this season by the Raiders are tied for their fourth-most ever through eight games and most since 2002. The 230 points allowed are the fourth most for the franchise in the first eight games. — Las Vegas has allowed at least 30 points in five straight games, one shy of the longest streak ever in one season. — The Raiders have allowed a league-worst 6.1 yards per play this season, while the Niners have gained a league-high 6.4 yards per play. — The 49ers have won six of their past seven regular-season games coming off a bye week with their only loss in 2021 against Indianapolis. — Brock Purdy has 99 TD passes in 56 games and can become the fastest 49ers QB to 100 TD passes, breaking Frankie Albert's mark of 65 games. — San Francisco RB Christian McCaffrey has scored a touchdown in six straight games. He can become the 12th player ever with 50 games with at least 100 yards and one TD from scrimmage. — The 49ers have won 32 straight games in the regular season and playoffs when not committing a turnover, tied for the third-longest streak since 1939. — San Francisco had no takeaways and no sacks in its previous game, marking the 10th time that has happened in the past 10 seasons. ------ AP Sports Writer Mark Anderson contributed to this report ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.headline: Irving and the Buccaneers visit Swift and the Bears in a matchup of the NFL's top rushing teams
headlines.description: — Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson knows a little something about a successful rushing attack. And he's impressed with Tampa Bay's ground game.
headlines.title: Irving and the Buccaneers visit Swift and the Bears in a matchup of the NFL's top rushing teams
headlines.linkText: Irving and the Buccaneers visit Swift and the Bears in a matchup of the NFL's top rushing teams
headlines.story: LAKE FOREST, Ill. -- — Chicago Bears coach Ben Johnson knows a little something about a successful rushing attack. And he's impressed with Tampa Bay's ground game. The NFL's top rushing teams face off when Bucky Irving and Tampa Bay visit D’Andre Swift and Chicago on Sunday night. The Buccaneers are averaging a league-high 168.6 yards on the ground, and the Bears are second at 150.8 yards per game. “I mean, I’m telling you, this offensive line is really good,” Johnson said. “The scheme is really good. They have a lot of variety with which they do things. Then the backs are phenomenal as well. It’s a potent, potent rushing attack. ... So that’ll be a huge challenge for us.” Tampa Bay's ground game was so good in Week 8 that it beat Atlanta 16-0 without completing a pass. Irving rushed for 170 yards and a touchdown in wet conditions as the Buccaneers set a franchise record with 324 yards on the ground. Tampa Bay is averaging 231.3 yards rushing over its past four games, winning three times during the impressive stretch. “I think we’ve tweaked some things, obviously, in how we’re running it and the things that certain guys can do well up front, as well as what kind of runs the backs can do," coach Todd Bowles said. “I think the coaches get more comfortable with the players and vice versa, and everybody is settling into the scheme and kind of buying in and being on the same page, really.” Tampa Bay's tight ends — especially Cade Otton and Payne Durham — have played an important role in clearing the way for Irving and Kenny Gainwell, who rushed for 140 yards against the Falcons. “The last couple of weeks we’re riding the hot hand with the run game, and it’s been great with the 12, 13 personnel and the heavier sets,” quarterback Baker Mayfield said. Chicago's ground game has slowed since a fast start. The Bears rushed for 785 yards in their first four games, averaging 4.9 yards per carry, and 421 in their past four, averaging 3.5 yards per attempt. Swift scored three touchdowns during Monday night’s 34-17 win at Seattle, but he finished with just 69 yards on a season-high 27 carries. Fellow running back Kyle Monangai could return against the Bucs after missing four games with thumb and toe injuries. “It’s been a little bit spotty. We stick with it though,” Johnson said. “I know first-half rushing hasn’t been as effective as second-half rushing. That’s one of those things that I know that eventually we will break through. We’re too good up front not to do that.” Need to know Tampa Bay (3-5) at Chicago (6-2) When/where to watch: Sunday 8:20 p.m. EST, NBC. Latest odds: Bears by 6 1/2. Against the spread: Buccaneers 3-5, Bears 6-2. Last week: Buccaneers beat the Falcons 16-0; Bears beat the Seahawks 34-17. Last meeting: Buccaneers beat the Bears 27-17 on Sept. 17, 2023. Series record: Bears lead 40-22. Matchup to watch Buccaneers NT Vita Vea vs. Bears C Garrett Bradbury. The 31-year-old Vea is one of the NFL's top interior defensive linemen. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 347 pounds, he helped the Bucs limit the Falcons to 99 yards rushing and 224 yards overall. Vea agreed to a contract extension in August. Bradbury took over at center for Chicago after he was acquired in an offseason trade with New England. He has started each of his 113 career games. Stats and stuff — It's the first meeting between Mayfield, the No. 1 pick in the 2018 draft, and Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, the top selection in 2024. Mayfield is 13-11 when facing a No. 1 overall pick as the opponent’s starting QB, including an 8-6 record in such games with Tampa Bay. — Chicago leads the NFL with 3,098 yards on offense. The Bears have the No. 3 total offense in the league, averaging 387.3 yards per game. — Tampa Bay cornerback Zyon McCollum is going for his third consecutive game with an interception. — Irving is from Chicago and played for Hillcrest High School, about 25 miles south of Soldier Field. — Swift has rushed for seven TDs in the past four games and a career-high 10 on the season. He has 48 rushing touchdowns in 97 career games. — The Bears have an NFL-high 22 drives of five-plus minutes this season. They also lead the league in average time of possession at 35:27. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.story:
In the final weeks of the 2027 recruiting cycle, ESPN's 2027 five-star class is settled.

Wide receiver Brysen Wright became the latest entrant among ESPN's 23 five-stars when the nation's top 2028 recruit committed to Miami and reclassified into the 2027 cycle on Nov. 5. Elsewhere, No. 1 overall prospect Jalen Brewster is locked in with Texas Tech. Ditto for top-ranked quarterback Elijah Haven (Alabama), No. 1 running back Kemon Spell (Georgia) and all four of ESPN's five-star offensive tackles. There's always room for late drama on the recruiting trail. But for the time being, everything is squared away.

So, let's break down the prospects who make up ESPN's 2027 five-star class. For each commitment, ESPN college football and recruiting reporter Eli Lederman and scouts Craig Haubert and Tom Luginbill take a look at how the nation's top prospects landed on their college choice and what to expect from them at the next level.

Jalen Brewster, DT

2027 SC Next ESPN 300 ranking: 1

Committed to: Texas Tech Red Raiders

Background: For the first time in the ESPN recruiting rankings era (dating to 2006), the nation's No. 1 overall prospect is bound for Lubbock, Texas.

Brewster became the cornerstone of Texas Tech's 2027 class when he committed to the Red Raiders last October over finalists Ohio State, Texas A&M, Oregon, Oklahoma and Indiana. The son of former All-MAC offensive lineman Robert Brewster -- a third-round selection of the Dallas Cowboys in the 2009 NFL draft -- the 6-foot-3, 310-pound Brewster has emerged as an explosive disrupter on the defensive line at Texas' Cedar Hill High School, where Texas Tech coach Joey McGuire won three state titles in 14 seasons from 2003 to 2016.

Brewster remains the subject of heavy flip interest across the country. He took official visits to Indiana, SMU, LSU, Texas and Florida this spring before closing his visit slate with a trip back to Texas Tech over the weekend of June 19 amid heavy flip interest. But the expectation remains that Brewster will be difficult to pry away from the Red Raiders. -- Lederman

Scout's take: Being disruptive along the defensive front was central to Texas Tech's Big 12 title and College Football Playoff run in 2025, and Brewster fits that identity perfectly. At around 310 pounds, he's a jumbo athlete who was nimble enough to also take snaps in the Wildcat formation in high school. His home is on defense where he can be a playmaker in the trenches, blending his size with an outstanding quickness, agility and power, which can allow him to anchor against double-teams while still being able to penetrate and disrupt in the backfield. There will be a year gap, but Brewster projects into a Lee Hunter-type role on the interior, but with even more upside as a dynamic interior pass rusher. -- Haubert

D.J. Jacobs, DE

2027 SC Next ESPN 300 ranking: 2

Committed to: Ohio State Buckeyes

Background: Jacobs, the son of former Georgia defensive tackle David Jacobs, and the godson of ex-Bulldogs coach Mark Richt, is one of the most productive high school defenders in the 2027 class.

The 6-foot-5, 225-pound edge rusher was credited with 102 total tackles and 16 sacks in his junior season last fall before he committed to Ohio State over Miami, Georgia, Texas A&M Notre Dame and Oregon on Dec. 29. A three-year starter at Georgia's Blessed Trinity High School, Jacobs will enter his senior season later this year with nearly 300 career tackles.

Jacobs remains the top-ranked member of Buckeyes coach Ryan Day's latest recruiting class despite persistent flip interest from Miami. He took official visits to Alabama, LSU, Oregon, Tennessee and UCLA before announcing his commitment to the Ducks on July 3. A two-way standout, Sabb will play wide receiver at the next level. He caught 59 passes for 897 yards and 13 touchdowns as a junior last fall while helping guide Glassboro to a second consecutive state title.

Oregon coach Dan Lanning has signed at least a pair of five-star prospects in each of the last two cycles, and the Ducks are on track again in 2027 with Sabb and Stepp in the fold this summer. -- Lederman

Scout's take: Sabb is a true weapon with the ball in his hands. He's really improved his stock with added bulk and strength to what was a very wiry, lean frame two years ago. He makes plays in space and can turn underneath routes into 80-yard home runs. This will also enhance his ability as a return specialist. He is very similar to former Georgia standout wide receiver Mecole Hardeman. Oregon is getting a game-changer in the open field who can play inside or outside and take the top off the defense with his 4.49 speed. -- Luginbill

Honor Fa'alave-Johnson, S

2027 SC Next ESPN 300 ranking: 21

Committed to: USC Trojans

Background: After signing the nation's No. 1 class and more in-state recruits than in any cycle since 2011 last fall, USC has kept its foot on the gas with local prospects like Fa'alave-Johnson in the 2027 class.

The Trojans made ESPN's top-ranked safety a priority in the early months of 2026 before beating Oregon, Texas, Miami, LSU and Notre Dame to Fa'alave-Johnson's pledge on March 14. A two-way standout at San Diego's Cathedral Catholic High School, the 6-foot, 175-pound recruit was credited with 40 tackles and three interceptions while totaling 1,530 rushing yards and 30 total touchdowns in his junior season last fall. Fa'alave-Johnson, one of nine in-state commits in USC's latest class as of mid-April, is expected to play on both sides of the ball when he joins the Trojans in 2027. -- Lederman

Scout's take: USC wants more speed, versatility and playmaking on the perimeter, and Fa'alave-Johnson checks every box. A 10.6 100-meter sprinter with good length and a wiry frame, he brings true top-end speed to a defense that's being reshaped around range and takeaways. In the Trojans' secondary, he projects as a versatile player who can play high, roll down or match up in space. Fa'alave-Johnson's quickness, ball skills and open-field elusiveness also give USC a potential difference-maker in the return game. In a league in which explosive plays and hybrid defenders are at a premium, his combination of speed, physicality and versatility fits exactly what USC is trying to build on the back end.-- Luginbill

Gideon Gash, CB

2027 SC Next ESPN 300 ranking: 22

Committed to: Texas Tech

Background: Gash, Michigan's top-ranked prospect in 2027, counted Alabama, Michigan State and Oklahoma among his finalists before committing to Texas Tech during an official visit with the Red Raiders in June. In the midst of an impressive senior season, Gash charted a massive rise in ESPN's prospect rankings in October, joining Brewster and Sweeney as the third five-star pledge bound for Texas Tech in the cycle.

Gash is the son of former Penn State and NFL fullback Sam Gash and the younger brother Michigan State freshman Samson Gash, the Spartans' second-ranked signee in the 2026 cycle. At 6-foot-4, 195-pounds, he's developed into a physical, long-framed, cornerback at local powerhouse Detroit Catholic Central High School, where Gash recorded 74 tackles, nine pass breakups and interception en route to a Michigan Division I State title as a junior last fall.

Gash has logged gameday visits to both Michigan State and Oklahoma this fall, and he remains a priority flip target for both programs. However, Gash is also expected to return to Texas Tech again later this fall and the Red Raiders, who have proven particularly savvy at holding onto high-profile pledges in recent years, are fully expecting Gash to sign in December. -- Lederman

Scout's take: Texas Tech's 2025 Big 12 title and College Football Playoff run raised the bar in Lubbock, and Gash is the kind of versatile athlete who helps a contender keep climbing. He's a 6-foot-4 corner with length and twitch, as his 4.2-second short shuttle and 21.6 mph of game speed show, and he's a legitimate college prospect on offense, defense and special teams. He's a productive receiver who can take the top off a defense, and he has already returned six punts for touchdowns, a Michigan state record. His natural ball skills and body control show up wherever he lines up. The Red Raiders will likely bring him in with a plan to develop him at corner, then adjust once he's on campus. The return game, though, could give him a path onto the field right away. -- Haubert

Kamarui Dorsey, S

2027 SC Next ESPN 300 ranking: 23

Committed to: Texas A&M Aggies

Background: The Aggies' first five-star commit in the 2027 class, Dorsey is ESPN's second-ranked safety in the cycle.

The 6-foot-3, 205-pound defensive back from Hampton, Georgia, chose the Aggies over Georgia and LSU on Nov. 1 in the late stages of a 61-tackle, four-interception junior season at Hampton High School in Georgia. Dorsey fielded spring flip interest from multiple programs, including in-state Georgia, LSU, Ohio State and Tennessee, but remains locked in with Texas A&M as a cornerstone within an impressive defensive back class alongside Henry and top-100 safety JayQuan Snell. -- Lederman

Scout's take: Texas A&M is emphasizing size, range and versatility on the back end. At 6-foot-3 with 4.52 speed, Dorsey brings a true safety body type with the athleticism to support the run, match up in man and patrol deep zones. Dorsey can play high or in the box, anticipating routes in zone and using his length and ball skills to generate turnovers. Coaches rave about his leadership and communication -- he already operates like a QB of the secondary -- and he's not a finesse player, embracing physicality as a core trait. In Mike Elko's defense, Dorsey projects as a multirole safety who can erase space, clean up in the alley and give the Aggies a high-ceiling tone-setter on the back end. -- Luginbill

headlines.description: — The Kansas City Chiefs started the season with five straight wins, nearly matching their total from all of last season, when their run of three consecutive Super Bowl appearances came crashing down with a forgettable six-win campaign.

keywords: New York Jets @ Kansas City Chiefs
headlines.story: KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- — The Kansas City Chiefs started the season with five straight wins, nearly matching their total from all of last season, when their run of three consecutive Super Bowl appearances came crashing down with a forgettable six-win campaign. Given such a debacle, it's not surprising the past two weeks have given some Kansas City folks an uneasy feeling. The Chiefs were waylaid in Seattle by the defending Super Bowl champions in a game that was never close, then went to Denver and blew an 11-point fourth-quarter lead in a 28-24 loss last Sunday that gifted the Broncos the top spot in the AFC West. “We've still right there, 5-2, and we've won a lot of football games. Everything is out in front of us,” countered Kansas City quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who has been playing at a high level less than 11 months after tearing ligaments in his left knee. "We just have to be better than we were last week and try to win a game," Mahomes said. The Chiefs would have a hard time finding a better get-right opponent than the Jets on Sunday. New York (2-6) has lost three straight, each a one-possession affair, and has struggled to stop anybody. And to make matters worse, star wide receiver Garrett Wilson was in the concussion protocol this week, offsetting the good news of the potential return of running back Breece Hall from a quadriceps injury that has sidelined him for the past five games. “We know exactly who this team is, we know exactly what they’re about,” Jets coach Aaron Glenn said. “They’ve created a sustainable winning situation over there. That’s a lot of credit to the players, the coaching staff and the organization.” In short, the Chiefs represent the blueprint for what the Jets have spent years trying to achieve. “Your record is your record regardless of what your roster is,” Glenn said, "and that’s the way that I look at it. We just have to keep fighting and keep having that hunger to try to finish these games. A lot of that comes with what we’ve talked about, of having that killer instinct. When we’re up, of being able to take a team out. When we’re down, being able to fight our way in to be able to get ourselves back into position. When you look at it, we’ve done that.” The Chiefs have spent the past week searching for that same killer instinct. After beating the Broncos in their season opener, the Chiefs had an opportunity last week to take control of the AFC West before reaching the midway point of the season. But their problems in short-yardage situations, another miss by kicker Harrison Butker, and tackling woes on the defensive side of the ball ultimately doomed Kansas City to a frustrating defeat. “When you have losses — critical losses — early in the year, especially with this one, it's about finishing,” Chiefs pass rusher George Karlaftis said. “When you're up in the fourth quarter and you lose, it's on the defense. I know I felt it. I know the defense felt it. "Scheme aside, I think that mindset of finishing on every single play and never letting up, I think that will benefit us greatly.” Need to know New York Jets (2-6) at Kansas City (5-2). When/where to watch: Sunday, 1 p.m. EST, CBS. Latest odds: Chiefs by 10. Against the spread: Jets 4-3-1; Chiefs 3-4. Last week: Jets lost to Raiders 38-33; Chiefs lost to Broncos 28-24. Last meeting: Chiefs beat Jets 23-20 on Oct. 1, 2023, in New York. Series record: Chiefs lead 21-19-1. Matchup to watch Chiefs RBs Kenneth Walker against the Jets defensive front. Walker started the season on a tear, but was held to 36 yards rushing by Seattle and 69 yards by Denver. He'll have a chance to bounce back against a Jets defense that allowed the Bears to run for 232 yards, the Dolphins to run for 156 and the Patriots to run for 148 against it. Stats and stuff — The Chiefs' Emmett Johnson had 128 yards receiving last week in Denver, the most by a rookie running back in franchise history. — Kansas City has won three straight against the Jets at Arrowhead Stadium, outscoring them by an 83-22 margin. — Chiefs TE Travis Kelce will be playing his 200th game on Sunday. — Harrison Butker has missed 16 kicks since the start of last season for Kansas City, the most of any kicker in the NFL. — DT Chris Jones needs two sacks to pass Tamba Hali (89 1/2) for the second most in Chiefs history. — The Jets have been outscored 107-9 in the final two minutes of the first half in 25 games with Glenn as their coach. — New York was 2 of 6 scoring touchdowns in the red zone against Las Vegas last week. The Raiders were 4 for 4 in such situations. — Jets WR Adonai Mitchell had a breakout game with seven catches for 142 yards and a TD against the Raiders. — Jets RB Braelon Allen ran for a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown against Las Vegas. — The Jets scored on their first six possessions — two TDs, four field goals — in their loss to the Raiders. They joined the 2019 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (against the Giants) are the only teams since 2000 to lose after scoring on their first six possessions. ------ AP Football Writer Dennis Waszak in Florham Park, New Jersey, contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.headline: Bengals' Burrow is looking to extend 3-game winning streak against Penix and Falcons in Madrid
headlines.description: Cincinnati's Joe Burrow and Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. experienced dramatically different lead-in games to Sunday's matchup between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid, Spain.
headlines.title: Bengals' Burrow is looking to extend 3-game winning streak against Penix and Falcons in Madrid
headlines.linkText: Bengals' Burrow is looking to extend 3-game winning streak against Penix and Falcons in Madrid
headlines.story: Cincinnati's Joe Burrow and Atlanta's Michael Penix Jr. experienced dramatically different lead-in games to Sunday's matchup between the Bengals and Falcons in Madrid, Spain. While Penix was throwing a career-high four interceptions while playing through heavy rain in a 16-0 loss at Tampa Bay, Burrow threw five touchdown passes and then had the game-winning touchdown run in overtime in a 43-36 win over Tennessee. Burrow has thrown 13 touchdown passes in a three-game winning streak for the Bengals (5-2) and will try to continue that momentum against the Falcons (3-5) at Real Madrid’s Santiago Bernabeu Stadium. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said good protection has enabled Burrow to thrive. “I think we have the most accurate and process-driven quarterback that exists and we have the best receiving corps — and that’s receivers, tight ends and running backs — that there is in the league,” Taylor said Thursday in Madrid. “All that stuff, we feel like we can really distribute the field and Joe’s going to do a good job of being the bus driver in that situation and putting us in really good spots. It allows us to attack teams in the pass game that way.” Penix will be looking for a bounce-back closer to the efficient form he showed when passing for three touchdowns with no interceptions in a 29-20 win over the San Francisco 49ers on Oct. 25. Penix said reviewing last week's game was difficult. “It was hard. It was hard to watch it,” Penix said. “But at the same time, you know, that’s what comes with it. You've got to own up to it. You've got to be accountable for the things that you did and the part that you played in it.” Early bird Coach Kevin Stefanski likes giving his teams ample time to adjust when playing an international game. The Falcons made their flight from Atlanta on Tuesday night and then immediately held a light practice Wednesday at the Real Madrid practice facility. Stefanski said he knows his schedule means an earlier arrival in Europe than some teams prefer. “This seems like the right amount of time,” Stefanski said. "We’ve done this a few times. ... I’ve always left a little bit earlier than most. ... But I do see the benefits of coming out early to a city where you can acclimate to the time zone, you can again be together as a football team for a few days, and it doesn’t hurt to be in a beautiful city like this.” Flip the script The Tuesday departure meant a quick turnaround for the Falcons following their ugly loss at Tampa Bay. “I feel like we have a cool opportunity here to kind of flip the script, traveling two days after our game on Sunday,” Falcons wide receiver Jahan Dotson said. “It kind of gets your mind off of it a little bit. ... We have a chance to redeem ourselves as a football team.” Bengals reunion for Bates Falcons safety Jessie Bates III was a second-round draft pick by Cincinnati in 2018 and played his first five seasons with the Bengals. “I think we all love Jessie,” Taylor said. “Everybody feels the same way about Jessie here. Always been pulling for him and really happy to see him be successful, Pro Bowler. He’s earned all that. Really easy guy to root for." Need to know Cincinnati (5-2) vs. Atlanta (3-5) in Madrid, Spain. When/where to watch: Sunday, 9:30 a.m. EST, NFL Network. Latest odds: Bengals by 3 1/2. Against the spread: Bengals 3-4; Falcons 3-5. Last week: Bengals beat Tennessee 43-36 in overtime; Falcons lost at Tampa Bay 16-0. Last meeting: Bengals beat Falcons 35-17 on Oct. 23, 2022, in Cincinnati. Series record: Bengals lead 10-5. Matchup to watch Falcons defensive backs vs. Bengals wide receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. Higgins had 10 receptions for 155 yards and two TDs in last week's win against Tennessee and was selected as the AFC offensive player of the week on Wednesday. Chase added 11 catches for 141 yards and a score. “Usually a team kind of has one number one guy and they have two of them,” said Falcons safety Xavier Watts. “It is an unique opportunity and challenge and we'll have to prepare adjustments and game plans to try to take away both of them, but it's a great opportunity.” Stats and stuff — Burrow leads the NFL with 20 TD passes entering Week 9. — Entering Week 9, Higgins ranks second in the NFL with 726 receiving yards and Burrow is fourth with 2,115 passing yards. — The Bengals have scored more than 30 points in three consecutive games. — Cincinnati leads the NFL with 288.4 passing yards per game and ranks second with 29.4 points per game. — The Bengals beat the Titans last week despite allowing a season-high 36 points and committing four turnovers, including three interceptions by Burrow. — Despite the interceptions, Burrow set season highs by completing 79.2% of his passes and by passing for 462 yards and five touchdowns. — This will be Cincinnati's third international game in the regular season following games in London in 2016 and 2019. — This is Atlanta's second consecutive season playing an NFL International Series game. The Falcons lost to the Indianapolis Colts 31-25 in overtime in Berlin on Nov. 9, 2025. They lost to the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-7 in London in 2023. — Bates has forced a fumble in three consecutive games. The previous Atlanta player to force fumbles in three straight games was linebacker Jessie Tuggle in 1990. — Bates has 14 forced fumbles, the most among active safeties in the league. — Atlanta's Bijan Robinson leads the NFL with 780 rushing yards, but has been held under 100 yards and without a rushing touchdown in four consecutive games. ------ AP Sports Writers Tales Azzoni in Madrid and Joe Reedy in Cincinnati contributed to this report. ------ See AP’s full NFL coverage here

headlines.story:
Five-star wide receiver Brysen Wright, ESPN's No. 1 overall recruit in the 2028 class, has committed to Miami with plans to reclassify and join the Hurricanes next year, he announced Thursday.

The 6-foot-4, 215-pound pass catcher from Jacksonville, Florida, gave his pledge to Miami over Florida and Texas. Upon his move into the 2027 cycle, Wright is expected to sign with the Hurricanes in December, joining Miami as the second-ranked member of coach Mario Cristobal's latest recruiting class.

Wright, one of the most coveted high school prospects in the nation regardless of class, is a junior at Mandarin High School and was credited with 77 receptions for 1,629 yards and 18 touchdowns across his first two varsity seasons. He entered the 2027 SC Next ESPN 300 as the nation's top-ranked wide receiver and the No. 7 overall prospect in the cycle.

A long-term target for Cristobal and the Hurricanes, Wright logged game-day visits with each of his finalists this fall, concluding with a trip to Miami for the program's 43-35 overtime win over Florida State on Oct. 17. Sources told ESPN that Wright's decision to join the Hurricanes early was influenced by the success of star wideout Malachi Toney, who led the nation in receptions and earned first-team All-ACC honors last fall after reclassifying from the 2026 cycle.

Wright follows five-star athlete A'mir Sears as the second five-star pledge in Miami's latest class, which began Thursday at No. 7 in ESPN's latest class rankings for the cycle. Between Wright, in-state standout Nick Lennear (No. 33 overall) and four-star Eli Woodward (No. 218), the Hurricanes now hold commitments from three SC Next ESPN 300 wide receivers in the 2027 class.

No. 1 Miami (8-0, 6-0) travels to No. 11 Notre Dame Saturday for a high-anticipated meeting of College Football Playoff contenders. Kickoff is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC.

headlines.story:
EAGAN, Minn. -- The Minnesota Vikings have once again hopped on their quarterback carousel. Backup Carson Wentz will start Monday night's game against the Buffalo Bills, coach Kevin O'Connell announced Thursday, because starter Kyler Murray is nursing a strained hamstring.

The change marks the 14th time the Vikings have shifted from one quarterback to another during a season, either because of injuries or for performance reasons, since Kirk Cousins tore his right Achilles tendon midway through the 2023 season.

Murray suffered the injury while running on a read-option play early in the fourth quarter of the Vikings' 19-15 loss last Sunday to the Detroit Lions. Murray also struggled to connect with open receivers throughout the game, leaving receiver Justin Jefferson so frustrated that he declined to speak with reporters afterward.

O'Connell said that putting Murray on injured reserve is not a consideration.

"I don't believe it to be much more than a week-to-week kind of thing right now," O'Connell said. "But for him, his movement skills and the way he plays the game, we do feel like we'd be putting him at risk of possibly turning this into a more significant injury than it is by trying to have him work through it here early on."

Murray scrambled seven times during a Week 4 game against the New Orleans Saints but has run only 13 times in his five remaining starts. But O'Connell said the injury would affect more than simply his ability to run.

"It's more the explosive movements, the quick-twitch movements," O'Connell said. "Running is obviously a part of some of that ... but it's more of just the overall ability to impact the game. And ultimately, we could try to say all we want of, 'Hey, you can play, but you just got to stay in the pocket.' But then football starts, and it's an imperfect game where he's going to react and we don't want to make this strain any worse than it is."

Murray missed most of two games earlier this season because of a concussion, and his QBR (44.7) ranks No. 26 out of 30 qualified quarterbacks as he plays on a one-year contract. Speaking Monday, O'Connell said that Murray would remain his starter this week if he were healthy. Asked Thursday if Wentz had an opportunity to earn additional starts based on his performance, independent of Murray's health, O'Connell said in part: "It's all about this week for our team."

Wentz has started six games and played most of a seventh since signing with the Vikings in August 2025. The team is 4-3 in those games, during which Wentz has completed 63.9% of his passes for 1,492 yards, nine touchdowns and five interceptions.

He has excelled in getting the ball to Jefferson, however. In those seven games, Jefferson has caught 44 passes for 615 yards and two touchdowns.

"[Wentz] is the perfect guy in a moment where you can't have Kyler out there at full strength to go in there," O'Connell said. "And we feel very strongly about when Carson's in there, we're going to get really effective quarterback play."
